title: aidd config
description: `.aidd/config.yaml`: how aidd advises in this repository. Every key is optional but `aidd_version` and `profile`.

extends.description: Parent configs merged first, such as an org preset. A child changes only what it names: a mapping merges member by member and keeps every entry, a list of named things merges by name, and any other list or a value replaces. A preset locks what it must hold.

locks.description: Set by a parent config: what its children may not set. An item is a key or one member of it (`docs.disabled`). A lock freezes the value, except `project`, which only tightens. Children may add locks, never remove them.

specs_dir.description: Where Spec files live. Default `specs`. A folder inside the repository, never its top: the Specs folder is a role's write area.

proposals_dir.description: Where proposals live, one folder each. Default `proposals`. A folder inside the repository, never its top: a change only to it needs no Spec. Keep a client's proposals in a repository only its cleared people can read.

product_dir.description: Where the product scope lives: `brief.md`, `brd.md`, `prd.md`, `outcomes.md`, and the intent order, `intents/order.md`. The Intents live in its `intents/` folder, `intents/INTENT-<n>.md`. Default `product`. A folder inside the repository, never its top: a change to any of these five files is a person's approval, never a Spec's, and a delegated push or merge never lands one.

dir.description: Where `aidd new <type> <topic> --spec <ID>` writes a linked document: `<dir>/decisions/NNNN-<topic>.md` for an ADR, `<dir>/specs/<doc folder or Spec id>/<type>-<topic>.<ext>` otherwise. Default `docs`.

disabled.description: Document types whose rule `aidd validate` skips, each with a reason, such as `{runbook: a library}`. `test-plan` stops the Spec's plan and the component's living plan alike. A type left out follows aidd's rule, the same everywhere, and `aidd validate` only warns. A child adds types, and `false` turns one back on, which a lock never stops. `docs.disabled` in `locks` freezes the rest.

items.description: A Spec file, repo-relative: no leading `/`, no `..`, no wildcard.

exemplars.description: The project's best Specs, which a person names, such as `["specs/SPEC-12.md"]`. Whoever writes a Spec reads them first, for their shape and depth, never to copy them. `aidd validate` warns on a path that does not exist. aidd never chooses them.

max_review_age_days.description: Days after a living doc's `reviewed_on` date before `aidd doctor` warns that it is stale. About six months by default. The living docs are the architecture overview, the data map, the vendor register, the glossary, and every doc a Spec links with `frozen: false`, except a runbook, which has `tested_on`. `reviewed_on` is optional: a person sets it in the doc's `---` YAML front matter each time they review the doc. A doc nobody has reviewed lately describes a system that has moved on.

max_runbook_age_days.description: Days after a runbook's `tested_on` date before `aidd doctor` warns that it is stale. A runbook nobody has run lately is a guess at the moment it is needed.

docs.description: Linked documents: where `aidd new` writes them, which ones `aidd validate` asks for, and how old they may grow. A lock freezes it.

approvers.description: The people an agent asks for a decision (`ask`), first to last: users, @org/team, or `email:you@example.com`. Empty or missing, the agent asks whoever directs it. Under `team`, the platform's review decides who may merge.

specialists.description: Specialist pools by name, such as `security`, `privacy`, `finance`, `compliance`, or `data`: the people an agent names when a change's risk dimension calls for one, so the right person reviews it. A pool that no risk dimension asks for, and that no area is named for (an expert pool takes its area's name), gets a warning from `aidd validate` and `aidd doctor`.

owners.description: Who decides: the people agents ask, and the specialists a risky change names. A lock freezes it.

agents.description: How the agents work here: which roles may suggest work nobody asked for, and each role's model, effort, and turn limit. A lock freezes it.

proactive_roles.description: Agent roles that may suggest work nobody asked for, always as a draft Spec with `suggested_by: role:<role>` that stays a draft until a person records `triage` (`aidd validate` enforces it). Default: product-manager (which also drafts Specs from incoming issues) and sre (which runs the retrospective). An empty list means agents only work when asked.

models.description: The model each aidd-team role runs on, as `provider/model` (`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`) or `inherit` (the session's model). Key it by tier (`reasoning` or `execution`) or by role name. A role's own entry wins over its tier's, so one role, such as the verifier, can run on any model by name. A key that names no tier and no role selects nothing, and `aidd doctor` warns about it. `aidd init --aidd-team` and `aidd upgrade` write it into each harness's own agent model field. Claude Code takes only an `anthropic/` model or `inherit`, Codex only an `openai/` one, OpenCode the whole `provider/model`, and Kiro and GitHub Copilot the model name. Where a harness cannot run it, the generated file says so: Claude Code keeps the tier's alias, and any other harness runs its own default. `inherit` writes no model field outside Claude Code. The aidd-team plugin carries Claude Code's own role files, so this key changes nothing there, and `aidd doctor` says so. Unset: Claude Code takes the tier's alias, and any other harness runs its own default model.

independent_review.description: Opt in to review by a different provider: the verifier and the reviewer run on a provider other than the developer's, so a mistake one model family makes is checked by another. Set the three roles in `agents.models` as `provider/model`. `aidd init --aidd-team` says when `agents.models` does not give that, and the lead checks the developer's `Assisted-by` trailers against the reviewer's and verifier's reports. It advises and never blocks. Default: off.

effort.description: How hard each aidd-team role thinks, keyed by tier (`reasoning` or `execution`) or by role name, as `agents.models` is; a role's own entry wins over its tier's. `aidd init --aidd-team` and `aidd upgrade` write it into Claude Code's agent `effort:` field. Unset: reasoning `xhigh`, execution `high`. Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL still overrides it. The aidd-team plugin carries Claude Code's own role files, so this key changes nothing there, and `aidd doctor` says so.

max_turns.description: The most agentic turns one run of an aidd-team role takes before it stops and hands back, keyed by tier (`reasoning` or `execution`) or by role name, as `agents.models` is; a role's own entry wins over its tier's. Unset, each role keeps the number aidd ships for it. The range is the roles' own (`max_turns` in the team's data). A project may lower a limit to its floor and raise it to the ceiling, the most aidd ships for any role, so a run always has a bound. `aidd init --aidd-team` and `aidd upgrade` write it into Claude Code's agent `maxTurns:` field, and no other harness's agent file has a turn limit in aidd's data. The aidd-team plugin carries Claude Code's own role files, so this key changes nothing there, and `aidd doctor` says so.

domain_packs.description: Domain packs to install as project skills beside the ones the repository calls for, such as `insurance`, for a domain no file names. Without the aidd-team plugin, `aidd init --aidd-team` and `aidd upgrade` write the practice skills and only the packs the repository calls for. Those are the packs a manifest's dependencies call for, the ones whose risk areas `aidd risk` matches on a tracked path, the one `project.compliance` brings, the ones this list names, and the ones a past install wrote. Each skill puts its description in every session's context, so a pack no one needs is left out. Run `aidd upgrade --yes` after you add one. With the aidd-team plugin, the packs are the optional aidd-packs plugin's: `aidd doctor` names the packs the repository calls for, this list included, and the project enables the plugin.

max_tokens_per_run.description: The spend cap of one `/aidd-team:autopilot` run, in tokens: the sum of each step's count from the harness, every token of its model calls, cache reads included, copied and never estimated. Once the sum passes it, autopilot stops and asks once whether to go on for one more cap's worth, so an unattended run never spends without a bound. Where the harness gives no count for each step, autopilot says so once at launch, writes each step's spend as `unknown`, and the cap can't stop that run. The default is about five large role steps, because one step on a large Spec spends about 10000000, mostly in cache reads.

max_task_retries.description: How many retries one Task gets before it stops and its Spec is blocked, until a person re-plans it. A retry is a fix after a red run.

min_fix_review_lines.description: The size of a quick-path change's diff, in changed lines, past which `/aidd-team:fix` adds the reviewer. A smaller diff runs one builder alone.

max_fix_lines.description: The most changed lines a quick-path change may have. It is the minor route's size rule, so a larger change is not for the quick path: it goes to `/aidd-team:specify`.

days.description: Days between two retrospectives on the loop itself.

retrospective_every.description: When the team looks back at how the loop delivered: after the days or the merges, whichever comes first. A Learn signal (a rejected Merge approval, a rollback, an incident, a Task out of retries) starts one at once.

max_paths_shown.description: How many paths of one area an `aidd risk` answer lists, with the full count beside them. It decides nothing: the route and the edit level come from every path.

max_intent_specs.description: How many planned Specs an Intent may list before `aidd validate` asks whether it is one problem or several goals. It decides nothing: a longer Intent is a warning, never an error.

limits.description: Named numbers that change what aidd decides or shows. A lock freezes it.

approvers.description: The people who run the team and answer its asks, as `owners.approvers` names them: users, @org/team, or `email:you@example.com`. The team's roles read it; aidd's commands do not.

areas.description: The areas the team works in, by name: a built-in area or one under `risks.areas`. A Spec whose Task scope touches one is the team's work. Optional: a team can own work by name alone, through the `development_team` of an Intent, a slice, or a Spec. A name that is no area fails the config's load.

harness.description: The harness the team's roles run in, as `aidd init --harness` names it, such as `claude-code` or `opencode`. A name aidd does not know fails the config's load. Unset: the harness of whoever runs the team.

models.description: The model each of the team's roles runs on, keyed as `agents.models` is. `/aidd-team:autopilot` passes it to a team's Orca worker. Unset: `agents.models`.

effort.description: How hard each of the team's roles thinks, keyed as `agents.effort` is. `/aidd-team:autopilot` passes it to a team's Orca worker. Unset: `agents.effort`.

development_teams.description: The development teams sharing this repository, by name: each one set of the aidd-team roles, run in one harness by its approvers, over its own areas and the work whose `development_team` names it. `aidd status --development-team <name>` shows one team's work. Not the `team` profile. Unset: one team.

standards.description: Standards: the team's own written rules and its copies of aidd's library standards (`aidd standard add`), each a Markdown document that agents read before a loop step, beside their roles' standards. Each is an opinionated standard, one choice your team commits to; an industry standard lives only in the registry. `aidd doctor` checks each path, role, and `enforced_by` name, and each copy against the library. A child adds entries; it cannot drop or redefine one a parent names.

path.description: The Markdown document that states the standard, repo-relative, such as `docs/standards/api-errors.md`.

roles.description: aidd-team role keys that read it before their step, such as `developer` or `reviewer`, or `*` for every role.

when_changed.description: Load it only for a change that touches one of these paths. Omit to load it for every change.

enforced_by.description: Names of `tests` entries that check the rule, so `aidd test` checks it. Without one, the standard is guidance a reviewer checks.

fills.description: The open choices it answers, each `<pack or skill>:<choice>`, such as `ci-pipeline:linter` (`aidd standard list` names them). Optional for the team's own standard. `aidd doctor` warns about a choice no pack or skill declares, and about two copies of library standards that fill one choice for one ecosystem.

from_library.description: Written by `aidd standard add` for a copy of a library standard: never edit the copy. To change the rule, write your own standard and replace the library one in `standards_policy`. `aidd doctor` reports an edited copy and drift; `aidd upgrade` refreshes an unedited one.

aidd_version.description: The aidd that wrote the copy.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the copy as written.

stack.description: The stack that brought it, when `aidd standard add --stack` wrote it.

standards_policy.description: A company's rules for library standards, usually in its org preset: `aidd standard add` follows them and `aidd doctor` reports a breach. Only opinionated ids: an industry standard is never excluded or replaced, only waived per project, with a reason and an expiry. A child adds and tightens: it cannot drop a parent's entry, require what a parent excludes, or allow a stack the parent does not. A lock freezes it.

require.description: Library standards every project must carry; `aidd doctor` fails while one is missing.

exclude.description: Library standards no project may add.

replace.description: A library standard and the `standards` name of the company's own standard that takes its place, such as `python/mypy-typing: typing`. Projects cannot add the library one.

allow_stacks.description: The only stacks a project may add. Unset, any stack.

items.description: A repository suite command. It has no new_behavior: red-then-green belongs to a Spec's own tests.

tests.description: The repository suite, run on every change by `aidd test`. Empty means a Spec brings its own commands. A lock freezes it.

command.description: Starts the app on this machine with its seed data (the command loads them), from a clean checkout, such as ["docker", "compose", "up", "--build"]. The verifier runs it in a worktree of the exact head commit.

url.description: Where the running preview answers, such as http://localhost:3000: the address the verifier drives.

preview.description: The one-command local preview: no hosting, no cost. The verifier starts it from a clean checkout of the head and records screenshots, a trace or video, and API transcripts under `.aidd/evidence/preview/<head_sha>/`. `aidd init` fills it only when the command is obvious (a Docker Compose file). A lock freezes it.

environments.description: Where a push deploys: each environment has a name, branches, tags. A push to one is `deploy.run` there, which asks unless it says `shared: false`, and a rule's `environment` sets the level. Unset, a push asks as `git.push` and a delegated merge defers; `[]` says none deploys. A child adds or overrides one by name; a lock freezes the list.

by.description: Who set the delegation, as `Name <email>`: the address you commit with, or your no-reply one. It goes into each delegated commit's `On-behalf-of` trailer, so it is public wherever the history is.

at.description: When they set it, such as `2026-11-04T09:05:00Z`. `aidd init --delegate` writes it.

decides.description: The asks the delegate answers: a list of `spec.approve`, `git.push`, `git.merge`, and `pr.merge`. `aidd init --delegate` writes every one a person can undo, and a later aidd adds an action only when you name it here.

reserved.description: Actions you keep, on top of the built-in reserved list.

default_branch.description: The default branch, as you confirmed it to `aidd init`, such as `main`. With no remote, the check trusts a branch only when this field on that branch's own tip names it, so a ref an agent makes is never the default branch.

review_due.description: After this date every ask defers, until you review the delegation. `aidd init` sets it 90 days ahead.

digest.description: When `aidd status` shows what was decided for you: once a session, or after each answer.

delegation.description: A standing delegation: the asks the delegate answers for you, inside these limits, on a passing delegate check. Only the default branch's tip sets it, a parent can only narrow it, and a reserved action is always yours. Claude Code is the one harness that answers one in this version.

allow_own_tools.description: Whether `aidd init` and `aidd upgrade` let aidd's own MCP tools run with no prompt: by name in Claude Code's `permissions.allow` and in Codex's aidd block. `false` keeps them asking: they allow none, and take out the names aidd allowed (listed in `.aidd/harness-rules.json`).

mcp.description: How aidd wires its own MCP server into each coding agent.

project.description: The project's constraints and rules, set by humans: a technology radar, the hosting, a budget, the team's own rules each with its why, and the waivers a person approved. Agents read them in Specify and Review; `aidd risk --paths` prints the rules that apply to the paths, must first. `aidd validate` checks them. A parent that locks `project` binds its rules, hold list, budget, and hosting. The lock tightens only: a child may add rules and raise a level, never lower one, waive a locked rule, or spend more.

work.description: Whose work the repository holds: `product`, the team's own product (the default), or `client`, work for a client. With `client`, a goal starts with `/aidd-team:propose`, not `/aidd-team:plan`.

stack.description: A technology radar: what new work uses. A child config adds to each list.

trial.description: In use on a trial basis: fine where the design says why.

hold.description: Not for new work without an ADR that records a person's decision. `aidd validate` warns when a Spec's Context or Design names one and the Spec links no ADR (a case-insensitive text match: a hint).

hosting.description: Where the project runs, in a phrase, such as "one VPS in the EU". Agents design and deploy for it.

budget.description: What running the project may cost. The SRE picks the zero-cost option that fits first.

max_infra_per_month.description: The most the infrastructure may cost per month, in `currency`.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of `max_infra_per_month`, such as `EUR`.

rules.description: The team's own rules. `aidd validate` fails on a repeated id and warns once a rule's `review_due` has passed.

waivers.description: Time-boxed exceptions to a rule. `aidd validate` fails on a waiver of an unknown rule or one an agent or bot approved, warns 14 days before `until`, and fails once it has passed.

defaults.description: What every product gets unless a person turns it off: each default is on unless `disabled` names it, with the reason (`disabled: {dark_mode: a print-only report}`). Agents build them on the MVP's Day 0 and whenever a change touches the area, from `aidd-team:product-defaults`, which owns each one and its test. `aidd init` writes none of them, and in a repository it detects as a command-line tool or a library (no web or mobile interface) turns the interface defaults off with the reason "no user interface". A child's `disabled` adds to its parent's, and `false` turns a default back on, which a lock never stops. When the parent locks `project`, a child adds none.

disabled.description: The defaults turned off, each with the one line a reader accepts as the reason, such as "no user interface". Every default it does not name is on.

dark_mode.description: Light and dark themes: the design tokens carry both sets, the UI follows `prefers-color-scheme` with a persisted manual toggle, contrast is checked in both, and a design spec's screen inventory has a dark column (`aidd validate` warns when it has none).

responsive.description: Layouts work from 320 CSS px up, with touch targets of at least 24 by 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8; 44 by 44 pt on iOS), and forms that allow `autocomplete`, paste, and inline validation.

i18n_ready.description: Strings live outside the code, dates, numbers, and money are formatted for the locale, and CSS uses logical properties, so a second language or a right-to-left script is a translation, not a rewrite.

perf_budget.description: A Core Web Vitals budget each page is tested against: LCP 2.5 s or less, INP 200 ms or less, and CLS 0.1 or less at the 75th percentile, checked in CI (Lighthouse CI) on the pages a change touches, with a JavaScript budget per route.

public_page_basics.description: Every public page has a title, a description, social preview tags, and icons, and the product has designed 404, 500, and maintenance pages.

api_conventions.description: APIs are versioned, paginate lists with a cursor, accept an idempotency key on writes, answer errors as RFC 9457 problem details, and send rate-limit headers.

data_conventions.description: Times stored in UTC and exchanged in ISO 8601, money as integer minor units with its currency, sortable IDs (UUIDv7 or ULID), `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `created_by` on every record, and a soft delete where a person can undo.

operability.description: Health and readiness endpoints, structured logs that carry the request and trace IDs, a graceful shutdown on SIGTERM, and configuration from the environment.

security_headers.description: Security headers and cookies: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, and Referrer-Policy on every response; cookies `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, and `SameSite`; CSRF protection on every state-changing form.

legal_placeholders.description: A privacy policy and terms page exist from Day 0 as placeholders a person writes (an agent never drafts the legal text), linked from the footer and the sign-up form.

transactional_email.description: Every email the product sends has a plain-text part beside the HTML, and an unsubscribe link and `List-Unsubscribe` header where the message is not strictly transactional.

dev_basics.description: A formatter, a linter, and a type check run in CI and in a pre-commit hook, a secret scan before each commit, an `.editorconfig`, one command to set up and run the project, a dependency update bot, and Conventional Commits.

api_latency.description: A latency budget on every endpoint: p95 under 300 ms for a read and 1 s for a write at the stated load, with a request timeout and a database statement timeout, so a slow query fails a test.

outbound_calls.description: Every call to another service or provider has a connect and a total timeout, and bounded retries with backoff and jitter, on idempotent operations only (`aidd-team:resilience`).

slo.description: A production service has an SLO, 99.9% of requests succeeding over 28 days, with an alert on error-budget burn (`aidd new slo`).

backup_restore.description: Automated backups of every store nobody can rebuild, a restore drill on a schedule, and a recovery point and time stated: 24 hours and 4 hours unless the Spec says otherwise.

request_limits.description: A maximum request body, upload size, and page size, and a rate limit per client: a body or an upload over its limit gets 413, a client over its rate 429, and a page size is clamped.

modular_monolith.description: A new project starts as a modular monolith in a monorepo: one deployable, modules by business capability under `modules/`, each with a public `api/` and its own data, and the boundaries checked in CI (`aidd-team:modular-monolith`). A client project or an existing structure turns it off with the reason or its ADR. `aidd init` writes it off in a repository that already has code, so an existing structure stays as it is.

compliance.description: What the product must be ready for. Compliance is on when `targets` names a framework or law: `aidd risk --paths` names the `enterprise-controls` pack, `aidd validate` warns for a threat model and an authorization matrix on security and auth paths (`docs.disabled` can turn one off), and `aidd init` writes the security-scanning workflow. The organizational work (policies, an ISMS, vendor reviews, training, a penetration test, the auditor) stays with people outside the team. `aidd validate` warns when a target that expects separation of duties (soc2, iso27001, pci-dss, fedramp, hipaa) meets the `solo` profile, which waives it. `aidd init` writes this table only when given `--compliance-target`. A parent that locks `project` keeps its targets: a child adds to them.

targets.description: The frameworks and laws the product answers to: `soc2` (SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria), `iso27001` (ISO/IEC 27001:2022), `gdpr`, `hipaa`, `pci-dss`, `fedramp`, `cra` (the EU Cyber Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2847), or `other` (name it in a project rule). Any target turns compliance on. `cra` leans on two controls most: EC-08 (scanning and an SBOM per release) and EC-18 (vulnerability handling). It needs a `support_period`, and `aidd doctor` checks the repository's `security.txt`.

support_period.description: How long the product gets security updates, which the CRA makes the manufacturer declare (Art. 13(8)). It is at least five years, unless people use the product for less time. `aidd validate` fails a config whose targets name `cra` without it, and warns once `ends_on` has passed. A parent that locks `project` keeps the later end.

ends_on.description: The last day of support, `YYYY-MM-DD`: the date the buyer must see at the time of purchase (CRA Art. 13(19)).

reason.description: Why this length fits how long people use the product. Write one when the period is shorter than five years.

writing.description: How the project's documents are written. It only records an opt-in for the humans and agents who write them; no check or rule reads it. A parent that locks `project` keeps its types: a child adds to them.

controlled.description: The doc types written in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: the objects (`spec`, `intent`, `proposal`, `runbook`, `postmortem`, `release`) and the types `aidd new` writes. Default empty: no type opts in.

risks.description: This repository's risk rules over the built-in ones (schemas/risks.json): its own areas and actions, and rules that add to or replace the built-in ones. `aidd risk --list` shows the rules in force and where each comes from.

name.description: The environment's name, such as `production` or `dev`, which a rule's `environment` names.

branches.description: The branches whose push deploys here, such as `prod` or `release/*`.

tags.description: The tags whose push deploys here, such as `v*` or `*-rc*`.

production.description: Whether this environment is production: a release file (`aidd new release`) records releases here when no branch or tag push deploys automatically.

paths.description: Repo-relative globs naming the deployable paths this environment serves in a monorepo: a Spec whose scope touches none does not wait for this environment.

shared.description: Whether other people use the environment. `false` marks the developer's own, where a deploy reports instead of asking. Name its branches and tags without a wildcard: a wildcard branch glob gives way only for the branch checked out, a wildcard tag glob never does, and `aidd validate` warns about either. Unset, it is shared, so a deploy there asks.

ref_globs.description: Git ref names or globs: `*` and `?` stay inside one `/` segment, `**` spans segments, and a name with no wildcard matches only itself.

folder.description: A folder inside the repository, repo-relative: no leading `/`, no `..`, no wildcard, and never the repository's top (`.`, `./`, or empty). A leading `./` and doubled slashes are read away, so `./custom/` is `custom`.

items.description: An opinionated library standard's id, `<group>/<topic>`. A registry id (an industry standard) never has this form.

stack_items.description: Technologies by name, such as `PostgreSQL` or `pytest`.

project_rule.description: One rule of the project, with the reason for it.

id.description: Stable, unique name, such as `money-in-minor-units`; a waiver names it.

requirement_level.description: How binding it is, in the BCP 14 sense (RFC 2119, RFC 8174): must, should (a reason to differ is written down), or may.

why.description: Why the rule exists, printed beside it.

when_changed.description: The paths it holds for. Omitted: every change.

enforced_by.description: `tests` names that check it. Without one, a reviewer does.

source.description: The ADR or document that decided it.

owner.description: The person or team who answers for it.

review_due.description: When its owner reviews it again; `aidd validate` warns once it has passed.

project_waiver.description: A time-boxed exception to one rule: a decision of a person, with a rule, a reason, and a last day beside `by` and `at`.

rule.description: The id of the rule it waives, or of an industry standard.

reason.description: Why the rule cannot hold for now.

by.description: Who granted it, in a Spec's `approved_by` form; never an agent or a bot.

at.description: When they granted it, such as `2026-11-04T09:05:00Z`. A person writes it.

reason.description: Why the rule is off here, in a few words, or `false` to turn it back on.

path.description: Repo-relative path to a parent config: no leading / or ./, no .., backslashes, or wildcards.

url.description: HTTPS URL of a parent config.

sha256.description: Required with url. Pins the content.

common.aidd_version.description: The aidd release this record conforms to; the method and the toolkit share one version.

common.profile.description: The profile (schemas/profiles.json): its risk rules on top of the built-in ones, which set when the agent asks for Spec approval. `team` asks on more routes than `solo`. A lock freezes it; a child cannot raise it.

common.identity.description: Who: a typed identity `<type>:<value>`, or a platform login (`@user`, `@org/team`, or a bare login), which is a person unless schemas/agents.json names it an agent or a bot. `x-who` says whether each type names a person or an agent, and `x-meanings` what its value holds. Any form may be qualified with a tenant as `<tenant>:<identity>`, and a type's name is never a tenant's.

x-meanings.agent: `agent:<harness>/<model>`: an agent, as its commits' `Assisted-by` name it, such as `agent:claude-code/claude-opus-5-5`.
x-meanings.email: `email:<address>`: a person, by their address, unless schemas/agents.json names it an agent's commit address.
x-meanings.role: `role:<role>`: a role of the development team, such as `role:architect`, which an agent plays. Never a person.

roles.max_turns.description: A turn limit: the most agentic turns one run takes. The floor leaves a run room to hand back, and the ceiling is the most aidd ships for any role. The roles carry theirs here, and a project's `agents.max_turns` stays inside the same range.

common.repo_path.description: A plain repo-relative file path: no leading `./` or `/`, no backslashes, no wildcards.

common.glob.description: Repo-relative path glob. `*` stays inside one segment, `**` spans segments, a trailing `/` matches a directory.

standard.choice_ref.description: An open choice, `<pack or skill>:<choice id>`, such as `ci-pipeline:linter`.

runs_in.description: The folder the command runs in, as a path in the repository, such as `packages/api`. Omit it to run at the repository's top. `when_changed` and `report` stay relative to the top. A folder outside the repository, or one reached through a link, is refused.

new_behavior.description: True when this command proves new or fixed behavior. It must fail on the base commit (red) and pass on head (green).

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock limit. A timeout is a fail.

smoke.description: In the config's `tests`: part of the smoke set, the only repository commands an emergency change runs (with its own). When no command is marked, an emergency runs the whole suite.

reruns.description: How many more times a failing run on head runs again. Every run is kept in the evidence; a pass after a failure passes, marked flaky, and the flaky test is a finding. A red run on the base commit never runs again.

when_changed.description: Run and require this command only when a changed path matches. Omit to run it on every change.

command.description: The command that runs only the tests the runner relates to the changed files, through the runner's own mode, such as `[npx, jest, --passWithNoTests, --findRelatedTests, "{changed_paths}"]`. It holds `{changed_paths}`, an argument of its own that becomes each changed path from the command's folder, or `{base_commit}`, which becomes the commit the branch left the base at, or both. A command with neither, or another word in braces, fails the config's load.

sees.description: The paths the runner traces to their tests, from the repository's top, such as `src/**/*.ts`. A changed path the command covers that matches none of them, such as a lock file, a config, or a fixture, runs the full command.

related_tests.description: In the config's `tests`: how `aidd test --changed` runs only the tests related to the change. It runs `related_tests.command` when every changed path the command covers matches `sees`, is a file in the working tree, and lies inside the command's folder; else it runs the full command and says why. A full `aidd test`, `--require-green`, and every red run always run the full command. Omit it to run the full command under `--changed` too.

report.description: A JUnit XML report this command writes, as a path in the repository (pytest `--junitxml`, Vitest `--reporter=junit`, jest-junit, gotestsum, cargo-nextest, PHPUnit `--log-junit`). `aidd test` reads it after each run and records the test cases that failed, so a red run can be told from "no tests found". A missing, stale, or unreadable report is a finding. The exit code stays the evidence.

covers.description: In a Spec: the Acceptance items this command proves, by id (`A1`, `A2`, ...). Optional; once any command declares it, `aidd validate` warns about an Acceptance item no command covers, and about an id the Acceptance section does not have.

common.test_command.description: One test command. Exit 0 is the only pass.

common.command.description: Command vector, one argument per item. Never a shell string.

common.decision.description: A decision, said once: who answered an action on exact content, and when. Every yes, and every no, in a file refers to it, and a decision that has more to say adds its own fields beside `by` and `at`, such as a `reason`. A place that refers to it lists `by` and `at` again, so that place stays closed to any other key. An absent object means no decision yet. An approval holds only by the commit that brought it to the default branch: that commit carries `Approved-by:` with the same person and `Approves:` with the item's exact id in its last paragraph, and changes nothing in the item but its `approval`. A field with no such commit reads as no approval, with an error. `aidd approve <id>` sets it and makes that commit.

by.description: The person who decided, in `approved_by`'s form, never an agent.

common.instant.description: A moment, as an RFC 3339 date and time, such as `2026-04-01T12:00:00Z`.

common.date.description: Calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. The pattern rejects an impossible month or day (2026-13-01, 2026-04-31, 2026-02-30) with any validator; February 29 of a year that is not a leap year passes the pattern and fails only `format: date`, which aidd asserts but a stock validator may treat as an annotation.

common.approved_by.description: The person who said yes, in git's trailer form, like `Co-authored-by`: `Name <email>`, from their `git config user.name` and `git config user.email`. When that identity is a bot's or missing, it is the `Name <email>` or `@handle` the person gives. An Approver's `@handle`, `@org/team`, or `email:<address>` holds too. It names only who: the head, the action, or a delegation goes in the commit body or the decision record (`aidd records add`). `aidd validate` warns about another form, and about an agent or a bot.

risks.areas.description: Named sets of paths, by area id. A rule's `area` names one, and a change that touches one takes its route and dimensions.

risks.actions.description: The things an agent does that carry a level, by action id, each with the patterns that recognize it.

risks.rules.description: Rules that set an action's level, narrowed by a selector. Of the rules that match, the most specific wins, then the higher level.

action.description: An action id, or a prefix that ends in `.*` (`git.*`), or `*` for every action.

area.description: Narrows the rule to a change that touches this area: an area id from `areas`, built in or the config's.

branch.description: Narrows the rule to one kind of branch: `own` (the agent's work branch), `default` (the repository's default branch), or `shared` (any other branch someone else pushed to).

role.description: Narrows the rule to one aidd-team role, by its id, such as `developer`.

environment.description: A name in the config's `environments`: the rule decides `deploy.run` to that environment, such as a push to its branch. Only a `deploy.run` rule takes it.

environment_shared.description: Whether the environment a `deploy.run` reaches is shared, as the config's `environments` mark it: `false` for the developer's own. A deploy aidd cannot name an environment for matches neither. Only a `deploy.run` rule takes it.

route.description: The route of the change whose Spec is approved. A rule with a `route` decides `spec.approve` on that route only. A rule without one decides every route, and replaces the rules a lower layer (the built-in rules, the profile, a parent config) set for one route, unless the parent locked them.

locked.description: In an `extends` parent such as an org preset: the rule is a floor. No rule of a child or a profile, and no built-in rule, lowers the level of what it covers, and a child's rule with the same selector keeps this level. A floor below a built-in level changes nothing there.

reason.description: Why the rule exists, in one line, which `aidd risk` shows.

risks.level.description: allow: the agent acts. report: it acts, then says what it did. ask: it waits for the person's yes, then acts.

description.description: What the action is, in one line, for a person reading the rules.

irreversible.description: `true` when a person cannot undo the action, such as a force-push, a deploy, or a message sent. `aidd risk --suggest` never suggests lowering its rule. Left out, the action can be undone.

commands.description: Shell command patterns: `*` matches any run of characters, and a pattern matches the whole command.

items.description: The methods in capitals, joined by `|` and followed by a space, or none; then the glob. A first word of letters that is no list of write methods, such as `PUSH` or `patch`, is refused.

api_endpoints.description: `gh api` endpoint globs whose write is this action, read from the call's parsed arguments in any flag order, which `commands` globs cannot do. This reads `gh api` only: a `glab api` pattern stays in `commands`. In a glob, `*` is any run of characters, `/` included, and `?` is one whole path segment, up to the next `/` or space. It is not one character, as in a path glob, and an entry cannot name a literal `?`. aidd cuts the query string off the endpoint before matching. A glob matches the whole endpoint without its query, ignoring case, or the endpoint and the call's field values after a space (`*dispatches*deploy*`); a file given to `--input` shows as `--input file`. Begin it with the methods it applies to (`DELETE */git/refs/*`, `PATCH|POST */git/refs*`) or with none for any write. A GET or HEAD with no field or input is a read. A GraphQL mutation, or a query aidd cannot read, is the endpoint `graphql#mutation`. `aidd risk --command` reads them as parsed arguments. A harness's ask rules do not use them: those ask before any `gh api` call that may write, whatever its endpoint, while `aidd risk --command` reads the call exactly. Redefining an action replaces the whole entry, as with `commands`.

paths.description: The files that hold secrets, as path globs: `**/.env` or `**/*.pem`. They are a fact of their own, apart from an area, which names the code a change touches.

exclude.description: Globs a read must not also match, such as a template `**/*.example`.

include.description: Globs that win over `exclude`: a read of one of `paths` that also matches one of these is the action, even when `exclude` matches it, such as `**/secrets.*` over the code exclude `**/*.py`. Claude Code's rules write each again after the carve-outs.

readers.description: The programs that read or print a file, by name, such as `cat` or `grep`. A command whose program is one of them and that names a file in the area is the action. For `cp`, only the files it copies from count, never the one it writes.

file_reads.description: Reading one of `paths` is this action: a shell command whose program is a reader, or the harness's own file-read tool where it has one. `aidd risk --command` reads each word after the program as a path. The harness's ask rules get a read rule for each of `paths`, and never one for `exclude`. Claude Code's rules then carve back out, with a `Read(!...)` rule each, the `.env` templates (`.env.example`, `.sample`, `.template`, `.dist`) and every other exclude but the template suffixes and `*.pub`, such as source code. Redefining an action replaces the whole entry, as with `commands`.

writers.description: The programs that write a file they name, by name, or `git` with its subcommand (`git rm`, `git mv`), each with the rule for which of its words is written: `every_file` (every word that is no option, as `tee` and `truncate` write them), `destination` (the last word, or the folder `-t` names, which a file copied into it joins, as `cp` and `ln` write it), `move` (the destination as `destination` reads it, and every source, as `mv` and `git mv` change both), `in_place` (the files after the script, and only with `-i`, as `sed -i` and `perl -i` edit them), `of_operand` (the value of `of=`, as `dd` writes it), or `remove` (every word that is no option, as `rm`, `unlink`, and `git rm` delete them, and with `-r`, `-R`, or `--recursive` each also as a folder). `git rm` and `git mv` with `-n` or `--dry-run` write nothing, and `git -C DIR` reads their relative words from DIR. `git rm` reads an operand with a `*` as every tracked file it matches, with the `*` crossing a `/` as git reads it, and an operand that git reads by other pathspec rules as a word aidd cannot read. A folder that `destination` or `move` writes into, when a source is a folder or `-r`, `-R`, or `-a` is given, and a folder that `remove` deletes, counts as every tracked file under it, as `aidd risk --paths` reads a folder. A program not listed reads as it does for any action.

file_writes.description: Writing a file is this action: a shell command whose program is one of the writers, and a redirection (`>`, `>>`, `>|`, `<>`, `&>`, `2>`) of any command, name the file they write. `aidd risk --command` gives the command the level that `aidd risk --paths` gives the file, so a write to a file whose edit asks asks too, and takes the stricter of that and the command's own level. A device (`/dev/null`), a file under the system's temporary folder outside the repository, and a file git ignores in one of aidd's own output folders (`.aidd/*/`) are no edit. A relative path is read from the folder the command was typed in, and no `cd` is followed. From a word that may change the folder (`cd`, `pushd`, `popd`, `env -C`, `sudo -D`, a command word the shell expands), also inside a subshell, the path is read by its name alone. It takes the strictest of the files and area globs that guard that name, and the answer says so. A bare name that only a folder-wide area guards raises nothing, and the answer names the file. A word the shell expands (`$LOG`, a glob, a brace) is left unchecked, and the answer says so. Redefining an action replaces the whole entry, as with `commands`.

tools.description: Harness tool names the action is, such as an MCP tool that sends email.

examples.description: What the action looks like where no pattern catches it: the agent judges these.

description.description: What the area holds, in one line, for a person reading the rules.

paths.description: Globs, repo-relative; `**` matches any number of folders.

exclude.description: Globs a match must not also match, such as `**/vendor/**`.

route.description: The least route a change that touches the area needs.

dimensions.description: The risk dimensions a change in the area has, which name its specialists.

action.description: The action a person's yes covers for a change in the area, such as `product_scope.approve`. `aidd risk --paths` names it in its next step.

deploys_on_merge.description: The area's paths a host deploys from when they change on the default branch, such as `vercel.json`: a delegated merge never covers them. Any area may set it, and the built-in `infra` area does.
